chunks: And through his chain of narration, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
He said: 'I have forgiven you regarding the alms-tax on horses and slaves.'

key_terms.الرَّقِيق: Slaves, referring to the category of enslaved people
key_terms.الْخَيْل: Horses, specifically referring to war or riding horses in this context
key_terms.صَدَقَة: Alms-tax (sadaqah), a form of obligatory or voluntary charity in Islamic jurisprudence

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet forgive regarding the alms-tax on horses and slaves?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, highlights a specific prophetic dispensation (*afw*) regarding the zakat on horses and slaves, reflecting the economic realities of the early Muslim community. In Shia scholarly tradition, this is often interpreted not as a permanent abolition of the tax, but as a temporary grace or a specific ruling for the Prophet's time, distinguishing it from the general obligation on other forms of wealth. It underscores the flexibility of Islamic jurisprudence in addressing the socio-economic conditions of the believers.
